ethics_check.title: Ethics Approval Check
ethics_check.summary_text: 1 of 1 paper appeared to involve live data collection and lacked an ethics approval statement.

table.text: The presence of age and sex information for the healthy donors of the Cristiano dataset allowed us to see the elevated scores within the younger female cohort, and our investigation then led to our hypothesis that those scores were likely due to pregnant donors who were recruited into the healthy cohort.

ethics_check.report:
Based on the following text, we would expect an ethics approval statement, but it was not present:

> The presence of age and sex information for the healthy donors of the Cristiano dataset allowed us to see the elevated scores within the younger female cohort, and our investigation then led to our hypothesis that those scores were likely due to pregnant donors who were recruited into the healthy cohort.

power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::

info.title: Detection of early-stage cancer using similarity-based classification of cell-free DNA fragmentation patterns

section.header: Creating an individual's position probability matrix
Outlier removal using healthy Mahalanobis distance
Representation of an individual's fragmentation pattern
Distance to healthy samples is a valuable biomarker
Cross-validation shows high performance in two datasets
Tissue of origin prediction accuracy is high
No evidence of batch effects driving results
Library preparation differences prevent direct comparison between datasets
Performance is stable at very low sequencing depth
